subject: How to calculate predictions for a linear combination in a model with an offset term?

messages.author: d4d48a3a6adf59bd
messages.subject: How to calculate predictions for a linear combination in a model with an offset term?
parts:
It is relatively straightforward to calculate predictions for a linear combination in a model without an offset term (see code below). However, I can't figure out how to calculate the same prediction for a model with an offset. The offset term doesn't get incorporated into a model.matrix object, and so I can't determine how to properly incorporate it into the linear combination. Thanks very much for your assistance!
   Judith

Reproducible code
# Artificial dataset of number of animals (N) captured in two sites (a, b) over time (2000-2004)
# The number of hours spent sampling (hrs) varies across years, and should be used as an offset
capture.dat <-   data.frame(N    = c(23, 20, 11, 15, 18, 28, 30, 23, 24, 22),
                            site = c(rep("a", 5), rep("b", 5)),
                            year = c(2000:2004, 2000:2004),
                            hrs  = c(5, 5, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 3, 4, 5))

# Fit basic Poisson model in INLA, without offset
mod.no.off <- inla(N ~ year + site,
                    data = capture.dat,
                    family = "poisson")

# Fit basic Poisson model in INLA, with offset
mod.w.off <- inla(N ~ year + site + offset(log(hrs)),
                    data = capture.dat,
                    family = "poisson")

# Now to predict the value for a linear combination that calculates the average across sites
# Manually create a dataframe that matches that output by model.matrix, but set the value for
# the factor variable equal to 0.5 to calculate the average
# Note I can't figure out how to provide a proper name for the intercept variable expect through
# this clunky method
predict.dat <- data.frame(intercept = 1, year = 2000:2005, siteb = 0.5)
names(predict.dat)[1] <- "(Intercept)"

# Convert to an inla.make.linkcombs object
lincomb.predict <- inla.make.lincombs(predict.dat)

# Extracting the predicted values for the linear combination is straightforward for the model
# without an intercept
predict.no.off <- inla(N ~ year + site,
                            data = capture.dat,
                            family = "poisson",
                            lincomb = lincomb.predict)
predict.no.off$summary.lincomb.derived

# But how to do so for the model with the offset?
# Assume that we want to predict the same linear combination as above, but with hrs fixed at 5
# If we naively proceed without adding the offset into the prediction
predict.w.off <- inla(N ~ year + site + offset(log(hrs)),
                            data = capture.dat,
                            family = "poisson",
                            lincomb = lincomb.predict)
# Then the predicted output is quite underestimated because the offset isn't included
predict.w.off$summary.lincomb.derived

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to calculate predictions for a linear combination in a model with an offset term?
parts:
there is no way to add an offset into the linear comb as of now, but you
can easily add it afterwards. It is just a shift in location.
I modified your example to do that. When I have to deal with the
'(Intercept)' I usually just remove it and use my own, as the code
shows.

I looked into the code, and there was no easy way to add the offset
consitently in the code. sorry.

Best
H
